The California Cycleway was a wooden elevated tollway built specially for bicycle traffic through the Arroyo Seco and intended to connect the cities of Pasadena and Los Angeles. Construction began in 1899 and about 1.3 miles (2 km) of the cycleway were opened on January 1, 1900. The cycleway was never completed, never made a profit and was dismantled shortly thereafter.

The California Cycleway's right-of-way later became part of the Arroyo Seco Parkway (Pasadena Freeway) in 1940, the first freeway in the Western United States.
